paragraphs.source_en: The first to enter the hall were Sanada Yukimura and Gotō Matabee Mototsugu, followed by Mōri Katsunaga; Masamori, the younger brother of Fukushima Masanori; Watanabe Kurōnosuke; Yoshihisa, son of Ōtani Yoshitsugu; and Susukida Kanesuke. paragraphs.source_en: The two priests, Paulo and Torres, together with their many followers, had entered Osaka Castle and become a pillar of strength for its warriors. A great many still firmly believed that Emperor Philip's grand fleet would come to their aid, and this hope kept the rōnin in the castle. The rōnin were acutely sensitive to the likelihood of victory or defeat; without this welcome prospect of reinforcements, most would have considered their descendants and abandoned the castle.
